rules: Work on features in order unless a later one is blocked only by an earlier one you already finished.
Only change the `passes` field. Never delete, reword, reorder, or merge features.
Set `passes` to true only after every step is verified by an automated test (Vitest or Playwright) that is committed and green.
If the spec and a feature disagree, the spec wins; record the conflict in open-questions.md instead of editing the feature.
docs/acceptance-tests.md is human-owned: never edit it. Implement each scenario as a Playwright test in e2e/acceptance/ that checks every expected outcome; never weaken or skip them.

M1.1 features supersede earlier features where they conflict (each names what it supersedes). Your own earlier tests that assert superseded behaviour must be updated to the new behaviour; acceptance tests are only changed by the human.
M2 features are appended after M1/M1.1 and supersede them where they conflict (each names what it supersedes). Update your own earlier tests to the new behaviour.

M2 never calls real external services: tests use local Supabase (CLI + Docker), the local-only test sign-in, and mocks for OpenRouter and Google Drive (see 'Тестовое окружение M2' in docs/acceptance-tests.md). A test fails if any request goes to openrouter.ai, googleapis.com, accounts.google.com or *.supabase.co.
Never run Supabase cloud commands (login, link, db push, functions deploy, secrets). The human deploys.
Visual reference for M2 screens: docs/mockups/*.html and the PNGs next to them; UI rules in docs/mvp-spec.md (M2) and docs/design-system.md.
Backend contract: docs/backend-spec.md (schema, RLS, edge functions, errors, test infrastructure). Deviations go to open-questions.md, not into the code silently.
